name: FinSearchComp
intro: FinSearchComp是一个完全开源的Agent基准测试，旨在对金融搜索和推理能力进行真实、专家级别的评估。该基准包含三个任务：时间敏感数据获取、简单历史查询和复杂历史调查，以复现真实的金融分析师工作流程。通过70位专业金融专家的标注和严格的质量保证流程，确保了其难度和可靠性。它包含635个问题，涵盖全球和大中华区市场，并评估了21个模型。
build_method: 三类金融任务分源构建, 70位专家标注, 盲审交叉验证, 动态与范围真值
eval_feature: 开放域工具使用, Global/大中华区双语划分, 78.6%范围评分, 专家抽查
build_method_en: Three Task-specific Financial Pipelines, 70-expert Annotation, Blind Cross-validation, Dynamic and Range-based Gold Answers
eval_feature_en: Open-domain Tool Use, Bilingual Global/Greater-China Splits, 78.6% In-range Grading, Expert Spot Checks
intro_en: FinSearchComp is a fully open-source Agent benchmark designed for realistic, expert-level evaluation of financial search and reasoning capabilities. It includes three tasks: time-sensitive data retrieval, simple historical queries, and complex historical investigations, replicating real financial analyst workflows. With annotations from 70 professional financial experts and a rigorous quality assurance process, it ensures both difficulty and reliability. The benchmark contains 635 questions covering global and Greater China markets and evaluates 21 models.

drawio_review_note: Paper-aligned against arXiv:2509.13160v1 Sections 2.2-2.6, Figures 2-4, Table 3, and Appendix C. The construction path preserves the three distinct source pipelines, 50 annotators plus 20 senior reviewers, reliable-source and ambiguity controls, 1-2-expert blind solving, and the final 635-question split: Global 337 (T1/T2/T3 134/119/84) and Greater China 298 (110/100/88). The 21.4% exact-match and 78.6% in-range values are distributions of grading rubrics, not model accuracy. The paper's score is a binary judgment J(answer,rubric) averaged as accuracy; T1 ground truth is dynamically fetched and evaluation occurs after local market close, while T2/T3 use static references. Human verification reports at least 95% agreement. Release audit pins randomtutu/FinSearchComp commit 55b6393fcf3c8f749ba5a69a70b20d4ef6f67caf (2025-11-02, after the paper), full data SHA-256 6437a6dae907ec81002bd817dafc26c3e46e6b6edfde700f22645b1e2aa208c4 with 635 rows, and AkShare subset SHA-256 9a0cf3a319fe3d154d54127f6f9d6bac8bbe5eea34d99167a3eed5add2d540d6 with 594 rows; bundled market snapshots are dated 2025-10-17, so they are not paper-time state. The pinned public evaluator has two material implementation mismatches that the diagram discloses rather than treating as protocol: its prompt requests scalar answer_score 0/1, but parser parse_judge_output requires fenced JSON and indexes answer_score[0][0], causing valid scalar output to fall back to -100000; additionally non_ts_total_score and non_ts_valid_evals are never updated, so exported accuracy remains 0 while original_accuracy alone averages parsed scores.
